vignette: A 33-year-old woman develops weakness of hip abduction and foot dorsiflexion on the right with numbness of the dorsum of the foot after a prolonged labor. The ankle jerk is preserved. Nerve conduction studies show a normal superficial peroneal sensory response.

options.text: Common peroneal nerve at the fibular neck

explanation: Foot drop with weak hip abduction (superior gluteal nerve) cannot be a peroneal palsy, and a normal superficial peroneal sensory potential despite a numb dorsum means the lesion is proximal to the dorsal root ganglion or in the plexus close to it: the L5 root or lumbosacral trunk compressed by the fetal head. The sciatic nerve would reduce the sensory potential and spare hip abduction.
